wave: CENSUS BLINDNESS -- project the resolved dependency closure into EngineeringGraph
wave_title: core::graph::engineering_graph had zero references to DependencyEdge/DependencyClosureReport. DependencyClosureReport was computed and attached only as a sibling top-level SystemizeReport field, never projected into the actual EngineeringGraph artifact -- a Closed dependency closure with real, evidenced package relationships (this repository's own 29 real edges, or a donor's thousands) produced zero graph nodes or edges for any of them, contradicting this contract's own stated rule that the dependency graph is canonical census truth feeding 'query, graph, security...'.

generation_model.G_n: 66b796d7de (fix(security): manifest-declared source roots cannot escape the repo root) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Moved to priority 3/4 (semantic preservation / census blindness) per the standing loop's own priority order, having closed the priority-1 (ADL evaluation) and priority-2 (manifest path traversal) items found in the previous two generations. Delegated a scoped investigation (Explore agent) targeting adapter/src/semantic/ (other extractors), runtime/src/normalize/mod.rs, core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs, and runtime/src/census/mod.rs for the census/extraction/normalization/graph pipeline silently losing or misattributing real semantic facts. It found and reported this gap with file:line precision, citing DEPENDENCY-CENSUS.md's own 'The dependency graph is part of canonical census truth, not an optional SBOM side report' claim as the contradicted rule, and confirmed via grep that no test anywhere asserts a dependency node/edge in EngineeringGraph. Independently verified every claim directly against the code before acting: confirmed zero references to DependencyEdge/DependencyClosureReport in core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs and runtime/src/census/mod.rs, and confirmed (by running the actual CLI before any fix) that `atlas-cli graph --root .` on this repository's own real workspace -- which has a genuinely Closed, 29-edge Cargo dependency closure -- produced a graph with no Package/Dependency-shaped nodes at all.

priority_classification: census blindness (priority 4) / semantic preservation (priority 3) -- a whole category of real, already-computed, already-evidenced semantic fact (resolved package dependency relationships) was invisible to the one artifact (`EngineeringGraph`) this project's own `FACTS_COMPILE_TO_ONE_ENGINEERING_GRAPH` and `GRAPH_BEFORE_CODE` invariants (both listed in `SystemizeReport.invariants`) name as canonical. This is not a crash or a false-pass gate like the previous two generations' findings, but a real completeness gap in what Atlas claims to have unified into one graph.

design_decisions.question: Change `build_system_graph`'s signature to take the dependency closure directly (invasive: ~30 existing test call sites across core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs would need a new argument), or add a new, additive, opt-in projection function?
design_decisions.decision: Additive: a new `pub fn add_dependency_closure(graph: &mut EngineeringGraph, closure: &DependencyClosureReport)` that mutates an already-built graph, plus a new `pub fn summarize_system_graph_with_dependencies(...)` convenience wrapper. Zero existing call sites or tests needed to change; the ~30 existing `build_system_graph` tests continue to exercise exactly what they always did (source/declared/normalized-semantic projection), and the new dependency projection is independently, separately tested. This follows the same minimal-diff principle as the previous generations' extracted pure-predicate pattern (`build_coverage_from_dependency_closure`, `adl_constraint_violation_blocks`) -- add a small, separately-testable unit rather than threading a new parameter through an already-large call graph.

design_decisions.question: What graph node/edge kinds to use for the projection?
design_decisions.decision: New node kinds `Package` (the consumer) and `Dependency` (the resolved provider), and edge kind `RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY` -- deliberately NOT `DEPENDS_ON`, discovered necessary only by directly testing against this repository's own real `.atlas/declared/system.adl`, which already declares ADL relations with predicate `depends_on` (e.g. `Runtime ->depends_on-> Core`, module-level declared architecture intent), independently projected to a graph edge kind of `DEPENDS_ON` by the pre-existing `SemanticFactKind::DeclaredEdge` handling in the same file. Reusing that string for Cargo-resolved package-level dependencies would have silently conflated two different evidence layers (declared architectural intent vs. resolved build dependency) under one indistinguishable-by-kind edge type -- exactly the kind of duplicate-semantic-concept collapse this session has now fixed multiple times in other forms (DependencyKind's Optional/TargetConditional collapse; the ADL evaluate_constraints/declared.invariants gap). Caught during this generation's own real-repository verification pass, not assumed in advance -- the initial implementation used `DEPENDS_ON` and was corrected after the verification run surfaced the collision.

design_decisions.question: Provider node identity: one node per (consumer, provider) pair, or one shared node per distinct resolved provider?
design_decisions.decision: One shared node per distinct `DependencyIdentity::identity_key()` (name+version+ecosystem+source_kind), reusing `ensure_node`'s existing id-based dedup. A provider depended on by multiple workspace members (e.g. `serde` used by both `core` and `adapter`) is one `Dependency` node with two `RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY` edges pointing to it, not two separate nodes -- matches how every other node kind in this graph (File, DeclaredNode, etc.) already represents shared identity as one node with multiple incoming/outgoing edges.

design_decisions.question: Where should `runtime::graph`/`runtime::code_analyze` -- which previously never computed a dependency closure at all -- get one from?
design_decisions.decision: Extracted the existing `NotApplicable`-fallback construction logic out of `systemize` (previously inlined there only) into a shared `resolve_dependency_closure(root: &Path) -> io::Result<DependencyClosureReport>`, now used by all three entry points (`systemize`, `graph`, `code_analyze`). This also fixes a latent inconsistency risk: before this change, only `systemize` ever computed a real closure: `graph`/`code_analyze` simply never had one to be inconsistent about, but a future change to the fallback logic in only one place could have created disagreement. One shared function removes that risk structurally.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every real, evidenced `DependencyEdge` in a computed `DependencyClosureReport` is projected into `EngineeringGraph` as a `Package` node, a `Dependency` node, and a `RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY` edge carrying its real `role`/`activation` facts; providers shared by multiple consumers are not duplicated; an edge with no evidenced role (`role: None`) is still recorded, just without a `role` attribute; a closure with no edges is a safe no-op; existing graph construction (source/declared/normalized-semantic projection, and the pre-existing ADL-declared `DEPENDS_ON` edge kind) is completely unaffected.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Five new tests in core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs: dependency_closure_projects_consumer_and_provider_nodes_and_a_depends_on_edge (full node/edge/attribute shape), dependency_closure_with_no_edges_is_a_no_op, two_edges_sharing_the_same_provider_do_not_duplicate_the_provider_node, an_unevidenced_role_produces_no_role_attribute_but_still_records_the_edge, summarize_system_graph_with_dependencies_counts_projected_dependency_nodes (exact count delta: +2 nodes, +1 edge for one dependency edge). All ~30 pre-existing build_system_graph tests re-run unchanged and pass -- the additive function touches nothing they exercise.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Ran `atlas-cli graph --root .` against this repository's own real, independently-computed dependency closure (not a synthetic fixture): before this fix, zero Package/Dependency nodes existed in the output; after, 11 Package nodes, 14 Dependency nodes, and exactly 29 RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY edges -- matching this repository's own real, previously-measured 29-edge closure exactly (`.atlas/evidence/verification/dependency-role-activation-separation.json`'s own validation recorded `edges_total 29` for this same repository). The pre-existing 3 ADL-declared `DEPENDS_ON` edges (Runtime->Core, Runtime->Adapter, WebUI->Runtime) remain present and unchanged, confirming the two edge-kind layers coexist without collision after the RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY rename. `atlas-cli systemize --root .` and `atlas-cli docs audit --root .atlas` both re-run clean with coding_admission unchanged from the prior generation (still only the pre-existing, unrelated WebUI materialization gap).

implementation.core_graph: core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs -- new pub fn add_dependency_closure(&mut EngineeringGraph, &DependencyClosureReport); new pub fn summarize_system_graph_with_dependencies(...); new private helpers dependency_consumer_node_id/dependency_provider_node_id (stable_id-based, matching the file's existing id-construction convention)
implementation.exports: core/src/graph/mod.rs and core/src/lib.rs -- both new functions re-exported at their usual levels
implementation.runtime_wiring: runtime/src/lib.rs -- new shared fn resolve_dependency_closure(root) extracted from systemize's previously-inlined fallback construction; systemize reordered to compute dependency_closure before building graph and now calls summarize_system_graph_with_dependencies; graph() now calls add_dependency_closure on the built graph before returning it; code_analyze() now computes and also reports dependency_closure (previously entirely absent from its output) and uses summarize_system_graph_with_dependencies for its own graph summary

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: dependency_closure_projects_consumer_and_provider_nodes_and_a_depends_on_edge -- full shape assertion: node kinds, node identities, edge endpoints, role/optional attributes
two_edges_sharing_the_same_provider_do_not_duplicate_the_provider_node -- exact scenario named in design_decisions: two consumers of the same provider produce one provider node, two edges

an_unevidenced_role_produces_no_role_attribute_but_still_records_the_edge -- a transitive edge with role: None (the real, honest 'never claim a fact this extractor cannot prove' case documented on DependencyEdge itself) is still projected, just without fabricating a role

real self-census of this repository's own workspace: 29 real RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY edges appear where zero did before, and the pre-existing 3 ADL-declared DEPENDS_ON edges are confirmed unaffected by the rename that avoided colliding with them

the same investigation surfaced two more candidate findings not acted on this generation: (1) EngineeringGraph.evidence is declared on the type but never populated by any graph constructor (build_source_graph sets it to Vec::new() unconditionally; normalization.evidence is never read by engineering_graph.rs) -- real, plausible, but lower severity than the dependency-closure gap and deserves its own focused generation rather than being folded in here; (2) dangling documentation-to-source path references (path_references matching a renamed/deleted file) are dropped with no diagnostic -- lower confidence, since path_references is already a known-imprecise substring heuristic, not a completeness guarantee. Both are named TARGET for a future generation, not silently dropped.

other Cargo-based donors in .atlas/temporary/donors/ would now also produce real Package/Dependency graph projections if census+graph were run against them (not exercised this generation -- this repository's own real closure was sufficient evidence; the donor corpus already independently verified the underlying DependencyClosureReport data this projection consumes, per prior generations' evidence)
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. Closes a real census-blindness gap: the resolved dependency closure -- already correctly computed, evidenced, and verified at real-world scale by prior generations -- never reached the one artifact (EngineeringGraph) this project's own canonical rule names as where 'the same typed dependency records feed query, graph, security...'. All three graph-producing entry points (systemize, graph, code_analyze) now project it consistently via one shared closure-resolution helper. A real naming collision with this repository's own pre-existing ADL-declared DEPENDS_ON edges was found and corrected during this generation's own real-repository verification pass (RESOLVES_DEPENDENCY), not merely assumed away in design.
